newsitem.title: UK: North Sea markets quiet, CFDs under pressure.
newsitem.headline: North Sea markets quiet, CFDs under pressure.

text.p: Although outright levels steadied following Tuesday's sharp drop, intermonth spreads and CFD levels came under some pressure on Wednesday.
One seller was seen particularly aggressive offering next week's (June 2-6) dates down from early sellers' ideas at July -24 cents to July -28 cents. Buyers withdrew as the offers came in.
On the intermonth spreads June/July lost some ground to -10/-7 cents while July/Aug talked a cent lower than earlier trade at -10 cents.
A mid-June Beryl cargo was picked up by a refiner at a healthy dated Brent +$1.00 a barrel.
Two Brent cargoes were passing through the paper chains on Wednesday and both were expected to be kept, traders said.
Other North Sea grades held steady with Oseberg assessed around dated Brent +15 cents and Ekofisk around Tuesday's traded dated +20 cent level.

Most producers and refiners saw the market as amply supplied and expected premiums to come off over the next week. They said Brent was being artificially supported by one player in order to cover a long CFD position but by next week, the value of dated Brent will have dropped "substantially".
July Brent traded at 1130 GMT up two cents at $19.24.
